strings.name: Greta Thunberg
strings.summary: Thunberg began a climate school strike outside Sweden’s parliament in 2018, helping inspire the international Fridays for Future movement. Her UN speeches and protests challenged insufficient climate action and turned scientific warnings into public pressure. She later joined civil disobedience and Palestinian solidarity campaigns, experiencing detention and fines for disobeying police. Her tactics and broader political focus also generated controversy.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected milestones do not constitute an exhaustive record of all news or controversies.
strings.influence.rationale: Launched school climate strikes and mobilized young people across borders, strongly influencing public climate communication and pressure on policymakers.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Mobilizing youth climate action
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: A solitary strike helped inspire international youth participation and increased debate over climate responsibility.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: International public advocacy
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Challenged leaders at the UN Climate Action Summit and other forums, emphasizing responsibility to younger generations.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Arrived at COP31
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Arrived at the UN climate talks in Antalya and urged leaders to prioritize people and the planet.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Deported after a Gaza flotilla action
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Was deported to Greece after Israeli detention during a flotilla attempt to deliver aid to Gaza.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Aid boat intercepted
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Sailed on the Gaza-bound Madleen, which Israeli forces intercepted; she was subsequently deported.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Fined for disobeying police
strings.timeline.event-04.text: A Malmö court fined her for disobeying a police order during a climate protest at the port.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Graduated and continued activism
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Completed secondary school and marked her final strike as a school student while continuing climate activism.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Named TIME’s Person of the Year
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Became the magazine’s youngest individual Person of the Year amid global attention to youth climate activism.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Addressed the UN climate summit
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Criticized world leaders for insufficient action on the climate crisis in a widely discussed speech.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Spoke at COP24
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Criticized inaction at the climate conference in Poland, raising the strike movement’s international visibility.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Began the school climate strike
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Sat outside Sweden’s parliament demanding government action consistent with the Paris Agreement.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Stockholm
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Sweden’s capital before entering international public debate as a school student.
